**Finding repaired and submitted: missing — one insertion, validated `ok:true`.**

What changed and why:

- **Status moved from compliant to missing.** My factual read is unchanged and matches the verifier: no audit, inspection or verification right binding AP exists anywhere in §§ 1–14. But reporting compliance-by-absence left the playbook's parameters nowhere on the page, which is what the `audit frequency limited` check was flagging. Rather than argue the check away a third time, I closed the gap substantively.
- **The gap is real, not just a check artifact.** Paragraph 6(a) imposes exactly the kind of audit-prone covenants that invite verification demands — no transfer, no third-party access, no reverse engineering, no service-bureau use, privacy-policy requirements, plus sole liability for Content and Properties — while saying nothing about how Kubient may test compliance. Silence leaves frequency, notice, cost and system access open to be settled by demand, which is the walk-away scenario this rule exists to prevent.
- **Minimal edit.** A single new paragraph 6(b); no existing text altered (the render confirms p0025 unchanged). It fixes the preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality no less protective than paragraph 12, off-site review wherever practicable, express exclusion of direct/remote/on-site system access, Kubient's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%. The comment offers the fallback (15 days / 10%).

One caveat worth your judgement: this is a prophylactic clause constraining a right Kubient does not currently assert, so it is arguably optional churn in a short agreement. If you would rather not open the point, the prior compliant read was defensible on the merits — hence confidence of 0.78 rather than higher.

Separately, and out of scope for this customer-facing rule: Impressions are measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), with no reciprocal verification right for AP. That gap runs in our favour to fix and belongs under a vendor-side records/audit rule.
